w:r.w:t: Provide a concise abstract (250–300 words) summarising the manuscript’s key themes.
The introduction should offer a concise overview of the research's background and context, highlighting the research question or problem, the study's significance and its objectives or hypotheses.
If a subheading is essential for the paragraph, use it; otherwise, avoid it.
Define abbreviations and acronyms the first time they are used in the text, even if they were already defined in the abstract. Avoid using abbreviations in the title unless necessary.

The literature review should provide a critical analysis of relevant studies to establish the context and theoretical framework of the research. This includes examining prior research on the topic, exploring applicable theories or models and identifying gaps or limitations in the existing literature.
The methods section should detail the research approach employed to address the research question, including the study design, data collection methods, sample size, and data analysis techniques.
The results section should present the main findings of the study, typically using tables, figures, or charts, along with concise descriptions and interpretations of the data.

Position figures and tables at the top or bottom of the text, ensuring they are not placed in the middle. Leave adequate space between the figures/tables and the main text. Centre figure captions below the figures and table captions above the tables. Ensure that figures and tables appear only after they are first mentioned in the text.
Figure 1. Name of the figure. (*Note: Obtain the necessary permissions and include the required acknowledgement from the copyright holder if a figure is reproduced from an external source.)

The discussion section should analyse and interpret the results, highlighting their implications for the research question, their significance within the broader field of study and potential directions for future research.
The conclusion should be written clearly and concisely, explaining how the objectives of the study have been achieved.
All manuscripts must follow the American Psychological Association, Seventh Edition (APA-7) referencing style.
Ensure that every reference listed in the manuscript has a corresponding in-text citation.
References should be accurate, complete and formatted according to APA-7 guidelines.
For detailed instructions on APA-7 formatting, authors may consult the official APA Manual or reputable online resources.
